summary: Tested TradeChart.jsx sanitizeCandles fix. Unit-level logic PASSES all 8 synthetic cases (outlier drop, 2%/5% normal volatility preserved, low>high dropped, negative OHLC dropped, empty/null handled, high-side outlier dropped). /demo-trade page loads without runtime errors (0 console errors, 7 canvases rendered, trade-chart testid present). HOWEVER, the outlier bug is NOT fully resolved in production: live /demo-trade still shows 3 outlier candles floating at ~1.128 disconnected from main EUR/USD (OTC) band (median 1.066, main max ~1.10). Deviation is only ~5.8% which is well below the 25% sanitizeCandles threshold, so they pass through the filter. The fix as-implemented only catches EXTREME outliers (>25%) and misses the visible-but-moderate cluster in real data.

ui_bugs.issue: Outlier candles still visible on /demo-trade EUR/USD (OTC). API returns 3 candles at ~1.128 (open 1.12845, 1.12674, 1.12475) while batch median is 1.06635 — deviation ~5.8%, below the 25% threshold so they pass through sanitizeCandles unchanged. See attached screenshot: cluster floats near 1.128 while main band caps at 1.10.

action_items: The 25% midprice-vs-median threshold in sanitizeCandles is too lenient. In the real EUR/USD (OTC) candle history, 3 outlier bars sit ~5.8% off the batch median and remain visible on the chart. Consider tightening the historical-bar threshold to something like 3-5% (e.g. median*0.95..1.05), OR use a robust statistic like MAD (median absolute deviation) with a multiplier so it adapts to legitimate volatility. As a safer approach: compute the interquartile range of midprices and drop bars outside median +/- 3*IQR (or similar), rather than a fixed 25% band.

Also consider filtering by |low - median| / median and |high - median| / median rather than only the (open+close)/2 midprice — some outlier bars may have extreme highs/lows that visually escape the main band even if their midprice is closer.

Root cause upstream: the VPS /api/market/candles endpoint is persisting outlier OHLC rows into the candle store. A backend cleanup script for the persisted store, or backend-side rejection of ticks that jump >X% from the previous close before they are written, would fix this at the source rather than papering over it in the frontend.
critical_code_review_comments: sanitizeCandles logic is correct per spec but threshold (25%) is empirically too loose — real user-visible outlier is only ~5.8% off median. Recommend using IQR/MAD-based robust filter.
Filter is applied only on initial fetch and pagination merge. If new candles arrive via socket 'candles/append' style events (if any) they bypass sanitize. Verify no such code path exists.
Tick guard uses lastCandleRef.current.close which starts null; first tick after reset is not guarded (fine for now, but noted).
loadOlderRef.current is reassigned every render (line 338), which is fine because it's read via ref, but consider useCallback + ref to avoid GC churn.

rca of the issue: The persisted candle store on the VPS (returned by GET /api/market/candles?symbol=EURUSD_OTC&tf=60) contains 3 legitimate-looking OHLC rows at ~1.128 while the rest of the 500-bar batch centers around 1.06635. These are ~5.8% off the median. The frontend sanitizeCandles filter uses a fixed +/-25% median band, which does not touch these bars. Result: the visual bug reported by the user (outlier candles floating far from the main price band) is still reproducible on /demo-trade after the fix. Reproduction: login (or inject JWT), open /demo-trade, select EUR/USD (OTC) 1m — 3 red candles visible near 1.128 timestamp range 1785196980-1785197100 (see screenshot). Mitigation options listed in action_items — tightening the threshold, using IQR/MAD, or (best) backend cleanup + tick-jump rejection on write.
